headline: Feedback is information about your performance—the signal that enables correction and improvement
universal_truth: Without feedback, you can't correct; improvement requires knowing how you're doing
fun_facts: Surgeons who receive video feedback improve twice as fast as those who don't
Immediate feedback leads to learning 3x faster than delayed feedback
Most people vastly overestimate how well they predict their own performance
discussion_questions: Where do you have good feedback loops? Where are you flying blind?
How do you respond to feedback—defensively or curiously?
What feedback would most accelerate your improvement?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Imagine learning to shoot baskets with your eyes closed. No feedback, no improvement. Feedback is the signal that tells you how you're doing—the information that enables correction. Without it, you're just guessing.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often resist feedback, yet it's essential for improvement. What makes feedback so valuable—and so uncomfortable?

options.text: Feedback closes the loop between intention and impact—you can't correct what you can't perceive; it provides the information needed to adjust course and improve
options.response: Yes. You might think you're doing well while failing badly. Feedback provides reality checks. Without it, you optimize based on imagination, not information.

options.text: Feedback is just other people's opinions
options.response: Some feedback is opinion, but the best feedback is objective data about results...

q1.title: Speed Matters
q1.script: Faster feedback accelerates learning. Knowing immediately lets you adjust immediately. Delayed feedback makes connection between action and result harder to see.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Speed Matters"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Specificity Helps
q2.script: Vague feedback isn't useful. 'Good job' tells you nothing. 'Your opening was strong but your conclusion was weak because...' tells you exactly what to adjust.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Seeking Feedback
q3.script: The best learners actively seek feedback—they don't wait for it or avoid it. They create feedback loops deliberately, even when the information is uncomfortable.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Without feedback, you can't correct. Improvement requires knowing how you're doing. Seek the signal.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 288. Tomorrow, we'll explore getting a little better every day—incremental improvement. Until then, create a feedback loop somewhere you lack one.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Feedback Loop Creation - Where Are You Flying Blind?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and create missing feedback loops
growTrack.activity: Where do you lack feedback? Where are you acting without knowing results? Design one new feedback loop—a way to get information about your performance that you currently don't have.
